subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host-local outbound media roots through a Telegram-specific config key, through a shared filesystem/media-root policy such as tools.fs.roots, or keep the current managed-root model and document it?
rationale: The requested key changes a public config surface and the host-local file-read/upload boundary, and it overlaps broader root-policy work that automation should not choose permanently.

options.title: Use shared root policy
options.body: Make the canonical fix part of a shared, security-reviewed root policy that Telegram outbound media consumes without adding a one-off channel setting.

options.title: Add Telegram-scoped roots
options.body: Expose channels.telegram.mediaLocalRoots with docs and tests if maintainers want channel-specific operator control.

options.title: Document managed roots only
options.body: Decline new root configuration for now and document the built-in allowlist plus supported staging and file-read-policy paths.

recommendation.title: Use shared root policy
recommendation.body: Make the canonical fix part of a shared, security-reviewed root policy that Telegram outbound media consumes without adding a one-off channel setting.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the outbound media access policy and root-resolution path that this decision would change.
